question_text: The graph alongside shows the percentage $P$ of radioactive Carbon-14 remaining in an organism $t$ thousands of years after it dies.

subparts.stem: Use the graph to estimate the percentage of Carbon-14 remaining after 4000 years.
subparts.solution:
When $t = 4$, $P \approx 60$
$\therefore$ there is about $60\%$ of Carbon-14 remaining after $4000$ years.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Locate $t = 4$ on the horizontal axis and read the corresponding percentage $P$ on the vertical axis.
step_by_step: Find $t = 4$ (thousand years) on the horizontal axis.
Move vertically up to intersect the decay curve.
Move horizontally to the vertical axis to read $P \approx 60$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Misinterpreting the scale of $t$ (4 thousand years corresponds to $t = 4$, not $t = 4000$ on the axis).

subparts.stem: Use the graph to estimate the number of years for the percentage of Carbon-14 to fall to $50\%$.
subparts.solution:
When $P = 50$, $t \approx 5.5$
$\therefore$ it will take approximately $5500$ years for the percentage of Carbon-14 to fall to $50\%$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Locate $P = 50$ on the vertical axis and read the corresponding time $t$ on the horizontal axis, then convert to years.
step_by_step: Move horizontally to intersect the curve.
Read down to the horizontal axis to find $t \approx 5.5$.
Multiply by 1000 to convert to years: $5.5 \times 1000 = 5500$ years.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to multiply $t$ by 1000 to get the answer in years.

subparts.stem: The equation of the graph is $P = 100 \times (1.1318)^{-t}$, $t \ge 0$. Calculate the percentage of Carbon-14 remaining after 8000 years.
subparts.solution:
When $t = 8$, $P = 100 \times (1.1318)^{-8} \approx 37.1$
$\therefore$ there is about $37.1\%$ of Carbon-14 remaining after $8000$ years.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Substitute $t = 8$ (representing 8000 years) into the exponential model.

subparts.stem: How long will it take for the percentage to fall to $15\%$?

mark_breakdown.desc: Take natural logarithm of both sides to solve for $t$
Obtain $t \approx 15.3$ and state final answer as approximately $15\,300$ years

subparts.solution:
When $P = 15$, $15 = 100 \times (1.1318)^{-t}$
$\therefore (1.1318)^{-t} = 0.15$
$\therefore -t \ln(1.1318) = \ln(0.15)$
$\therefore t = \frac{\ln(0.15)}{-\ln(1.1318)} \approx 15.3$
$\therefore$ it will take approximately $15\,300$ years for the percentage of Carbon-14 to fall to $15\%$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: To solve an exponential equation $a^u = b$ for an unknown in the exponent, take the logarithm of both sides.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Negative sign error when solving for $t$, or leaving the final answer as 15.3 instead of converting to actual years.
